title: One-Sided Randomized Recognition Lies in NP
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If a polynomial-time verifier using a polynomial number of uniformly random bits accepts each member with probability at least $2/3$ and never accepts a nonmember, then $L$ belongs to $	extsf{NP}$: there are constants $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a polynomial-time decidable language $V$ such that $x\in L$ exactly when some string $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ has $x\mathbin{++}u\in V$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
The number of random bits is $a(n+1)^k$ for some natural numbers $a,k$
Acceptance probability is at least $2/3$ for members
Every random string yields rejection for nonmembers
